new_statements.quote: Nothing is known about the prosodic features of Albanian. Nevertheless, the strong presence of enclitic (in parts also proclitic) elements suggests that the language was characterised by some kind of stress accent.
new_statements.citation: Gippert, Jost & Wolfgang Schulze. 2023. The Language of the Caucasian Albanians. In Jost Gippert & Jasmine Dum-Tragut (eds.), Caucasian Albania: An International Handbook, 167-229. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter. DOI 10.1515/9783110794687-004
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (753 pp., De Gruyter 2023, OAPEN mirror). Printed p. 177 = PDF page 194, running head "The Language of the Caucasian Albanians 177", within ch. 4 (Gippert & Schulze; chapter DOI https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110794687-004 printed on its opening page). Sect. 2.2.3 "Syllable structure and prosody" ends with the sentence exactly as quoted: "Nothing is known about the prosodic features of Albanian. Nevertheless, the strong presence of enclitic (in parts also proclitic) elements suggests that the language was characterised by some kind of stress accent." The rest of the section is on syllable structure (cluster avoidance, anaptyxis/metathesis in loans, status of pharyngeal <ʕ>); sect. 2.2.4…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The primary describers state explicitly that nothing is known about Caucasian Albanian prosody; they infer only that the language probably had a stress accent (from the abundance of clitics), without any statement of where it fell. A passing remark in ch. 5 (Schulze & Gippert, p. 255) that clitics came to stand 'after the first accented syllable of the verbal complex' is an inference used to explain endoclisis, not a placement rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the source says the prosody is unknown.
new_statements.domain_note: Extinct corpus language (7th-c. palimpsests, Mingachevir inscriptions); stress is not recoverable from the script. The only indirect evidence cited is clitic placement in the verbal complex (word/verbal-complex level).
new_statements.identity_note: Aghwan = Caucasian Albanian = Old Udi (ISO xag), the language of the 7th-c. Sinai palimpsests (Sin. N 13, N 55) and the Mingachevir inscriptions; an extinct Lezgic language, ancestor of or sister to modern Udi (udii1243). The statement is about the palimpsest language as a whole (no dialects distinguished). The handbook chapter is the same authors' (Gippert & Schulze) condensation of the 2008 Brepols edition's grammar sketch.

sources.quote: Nothing is known about the prosodic features of Albanian. Nevertheless, the strong presence of enclitic (in parts also proclitic) elements suggests that the language was characterised by some kind of stress accent.
sources.note: Sect. 2.2.3 'Syllable structure and prosody', p. 177: nothing is known about Albanian prosody; the abundance of enclitic/proclitic elements suggests the language had some kind of stress accent. No placement rule. Ch. 5 (Schulze & Gippert, pp. 231-260), p. 255, adds in passing that clitics came to be placed 'after the first accented syllable of the verbal complex'.
